intervals.label: approval and construction
intervals.note: The paper says construction of the spectrometer started after CERN approved the experiment in October 1998, followed by a technical run in 2001; the end bound (2001) is year precision.
intervals.quote: started after the experiment approval by CERN in October 1998

intervals.label: physics data taking
intervals.locator: arXiv:hep-ex/0703049 abstract; CERN COMPASS page: "last run in 2021-2022"
intervals.note: Physics data taking from 2002 (muon beam; hadron beam in 2004), resumed in 2006 after the 2005 accelerator shutdown; last run in 2021-2022 per the CERN page.
intervals.quote: The setup has been successfully operated from 2002 onwards using a muon beam.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: Year precision: last run in 2021-2022; AMBER page: "the COMPASS experiment, which concluded in 2022".
intervals.quote: AMBER, or Apparatus for Meson and Baryon Experimental Research, will be the next-generation successor of COMPASS after the experiment’s last run in 2021–2022.

placements.note: EHN2 per the AMBER letter of intent.
placements.quote: using the existing spectrometer in EHN2

summary.plain: A two-stage magnetic spectrometer with a large polarised target, tracking chambers, a ring-imaging Cherenkov counter and calorimeters, built to follow all particles from beam collisions with a target.
summary.technical: COMPASS: polarised target in a superconducting solenoid (muon beam), two-stage large-angle / large-momentum spectrometer with several types of tracking detectors, RICH counter, hadron and electromagnetic calorimeters and muon filters; reused as the AMBER backbone.

technology.quote: Outgoing particles are detected by a two-stage, large angle and large momentum range spectrometer.
technology.value: Two-stage, large-angle and large-momentum-range magnetic spectrometer with polarised target, RICH and calorimeters
